key_insight: ScaFE turns an LLM into a medical feature engineer, converting scar-assessment knowledge into explicit image features instead of using the model as a black-box classifier.
clinical_relevance: This could help scar classification when labeled data are scarce, while keeping image processing local and making outputs easier for clinicians to interpret.
method: Prompt the LLM with established scar assessment criteria.
Have it generate deterministic Python code for feature extraction.
Map images into clinically aligned features such as Vancouver Scar Scale components.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the method is reported to outperform end-to-end deep learning and black-box LLM baselines under limited-data scar classification settings.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the prompt and the validity of the generated features, so robustness and generalizability need careful validation before clinical use.
paper_title: When LLMs Analyze Scars: From Images to Clinically-Meaningful Features
